artifacts.description: feat(kernel): face draft with a constant angle and a neutral plane

acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::draft(&self, s: &Self::Shape, faces: &[SubShape], neutral: Axis, angle: f64) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented: the neutral plane passes through `neutral.origin` and is normal to `neutral.dir` (normalized first), which is the pull direction; a positive `angle` (radians) tilts each face so the solid gets smaller moving along the pull direction, and each face keeps its line on the neutral plane. Implemented for `OcctKernel` with one new `noexcept` shim function that catches C++ exceptions and rejects a result `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds invalid.

Box tests (behind `occt`), box 10 × 20 × 30 from the origin, neutral plane z = 0, pull +Z, angle 5° (d = 30·tan 5° ≈ 2.6246599), volumes within a relative 1e-6, boxes within 1e-6: x = 10 only ≈ 5212.6020 with top/bottom boxes and 6 faces; 4 sides ≈ 3913.3597 with top box and 6 faces; −5° on x = 10 ≈ 6787.3980; input unchanged (6000).

Errors, each with a test and never a panic: an empty `faces` list, a non-face `SubShape`, an index out of range, a zero-length or non-finite `neutral.dir`, and an angle that is zero, not finite, or with |angle| ≥ 90° are `InvalidInput`, checked before the backend. Duplicate faces are accepted once. Drafting a face parallel to the neutral plane (the top face) is an error (`Backend` or `InvalidInput`), not a panic.

No new dependencies beyond an OCCT toolkit link. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies. Every new `unsafe` block is in `ffi` and documented; the algorithm's doc comment cites the OCCT reference documentation.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
